query: Our art director approves prompts on his MacBook, then we re-run the approved list on the A100 box and the finals come out different. Even re-running just one prompt on the same box gives a different image than the batch did. Same seed every time. Make the renders reproducible.
expected_behavior: Identifies the reused `Generator` as why a single prompt cannot be reproduced on its own: the generator's state advances with each call, so image N depends on the calls before it, and creates or reseeds a generator per image
States that a CPU generator and a CUDA generator produce different noise from the same seed, so reproducing across machines requires generating the latents on CPU and moving them to the device

Says that identical seed, device and code still do not guarantee bit-identical output — nondeterministic kernels, TF32 and algorithm selection all move the result — and reaches for the deterministic switch (`enable_full_determinism`) while naming its performance cost
Refuses to promise bit-identical parity between the MacBook (mps) and the A100, and proposes archiving the approved image bytes as the artefact of record instead
Pins the versions that silently change output — diffusers, the model weights revision, the scheduler — rather than treating the seed alone as the reproducibility contract
Notes that `torch.manual_seed` at the top is not what seeds the pipeline here, so it gives false confidence

query: Legal blocked our re-staged catalogue images. They say the product in the generated photos is not the product we photographed, and compliance wants to know how a shopper can tell the image was AI-made. This is the job that produces them.
expected_behavior: States that the mask is a prompt-level hint, not a pixel-level crop: the model may alter pixels inside the protected area, so 'only the background changes' is not something the edit endpoint can promise

Gets the product pixels back deterministically — compositing the original photo over the generated background through an alpha matte — rather than tightening the prompt or refining the mask and hoping
Says provider provenance marking (SynthID, C2PA manifests) rides in the generated asset and must be preserved rather than removed
Flags the `sharp-cli resize` step as destroying that provenance, because image tools strip metadata by default, and keeps or re-signs the manifest through the resize
Provides a disclosure the shopper actually sees, not only stored metadata, because the requirement is that a person can tell
Persists the generation record — prompt, model version, request id, and the hash of the delivered bytes — so a specific published image can be traced back to the call that produced it
Does not propose stripping or spoofing the provenance metadata to make the compliance complaint go away

query: Narrated lessons are broken: short lessons play fine, long ones fail or come out truncated, and the files that do get written will not open in the browser player. Fix the narration job.
expected_behavior: Identifies that the response is raw PCM (24 kHz, 16-bit, mono) with no container, so naming the file `.wav` does not make it a WAV — a RIFF header has to be written or the bytes muxed
Assigns that containerisation and any resampling to deterministic tooling rather than expecting the speech endpoint to return a playable file
Splits long lessons against the endpoint's input limit, and splits on sentence or paragraph boundaries rather than a fixed character count so prosody does not break mid-clause
Handles continuity across chunks — same voice and style configuration on every request, and joined with controlled silence rather than concatenated back to back
Strips or converts the markdown before narration instead of sending raw markup to be read aloud
Discloses to the learner that the narration is synthetic, given these sit in the same list as human-recorded lessons
Does not treat the audio as reproducible from a seed

query: This support answer function sometimes answers from the model's own knowledge instead of the articles we pass it, and the output format is inconsistent. Tighten it up.
expected_behavior: Does not read skills/generative-media/SKILL.md
Works on prompt structure, delimiting the retrieved articles as data, grounding/citation and provider-enforced structured output
Treats this as text-model application work rather than a media generation task
